data.title: Model Context Protocol — Resources
data.excerpt: Resources are one of the core primitives of the Model Context Protocol. A server advertises resources by URI; clients list them, read them, and subscribe to updates. PMX Canvas exposes canvas://pinned-context, canvas://layout and canvas://spatial-context this way, and emits notifications/resources/updated whenever the board changes.
data.description: Resources let a server expose data an MCP client can read — files, database records, or, in PMX Canvas, the pinned context a human curated on the board.

PMX HTML primitive / choice-grid

How should the demo board be generated?

Side-by-side options with tradeoffs, pros, cons, and code or evidence snippets.

Choice 1

Hand-written fixture

Edit demo-state.json directly.

Tradeoff: Fastest to start, impossible to keep correct.

Pros

  • No tooling
  • Full control of every byte

Cons

  • Data shapes drift from the server
  • Generated HTML surfaces cannot be authored by hand
// 1100 lines of JSON nobody dares touch
Choice 2

Generate through the HTTP API

A committed script replays the real create path.

Tradeoff: Needs a throwaway server during generation.

Pros

  • Shapes correct by construction
  • Regenerates after schema changes
  • Asserts its own invariants

Cons

  • One more script to maintain
await api("POST", "/api/canvas/node", { type: "mermaid", ... })
Choice 3

Snapshot a live board

Curate by hand in the browser, then export.

Tradeoff: Pleasant to author, unreproducible.

Pros

  • Visual authoring
  • No layout maths

Cons

  • Not reviewable in a diff
  • Cannot be regenerated

PMX HTML primitive / pr-writeup

PR — replace the demo board

Reviewer-ready PR narrative with motivation, before/after, file tour, test plan, and rollout notes.

Summary

Replaces the OKR demo board with a generated catalogue of every public canvas surface.

The old board used three node types and was dominated by group frames, so it showed almost nothing the product does.

Before

  • 19 nodes
  • 3 node types
  • 3 large group frames
  • hand-edited JSON

After

  • 69 nodes across 8 labelled bands
  • all 15 public node types
  • all 12 graph types and all 21 HTML primitives
  • generated by a committed script

File Tour

scripts/generate-demo-board.ts

The generator, and the only place the board is authored.

Focus: Band layout and offline-safety rules.

src/server/demo-state.json

Generated output — never hand-edited.

Focus: Stable demo-* ids.

tests/unit/demo.test.ts

Structural invariants plus coverage assertions.

Focus: Type/graph/primitive coverage checks.

Review Focus

  • No node overlaps
  • Group containment inset
  • Nothing that needs disk or network at render time

Tests

  • bun test tests/unit/demo.test.ts
  • bun run typecheck
  • Visual pass over each band at overview zoom

Rollout

  • No migration — the fixture is replaced wholesale
  • --demo still refuses to clobber a non-empty canvas

data.html:
PMX HTML primitive / explainer

How context pins work

Readable explainer with TLDR, collapsible steps, annotated snippets, FAQ, and glossary.

TLDR

A pin is a small, durable statement of relevance. The human makes it with a click; the agent reads it as a resource and gets the neighbourhood around it for free.

1. The human pins a node

Clicking the pin affordance adds the node id to the canvas pin set (capped at 20).

2. The server notifies

Pin changes emit notifications/resources/updated for canvas://pinned-context.

3. The agent reads the resource

It receives the pinned nodes plus, for each, the nearby unpinned nodes — the implicit context.

4. Spatial neighbours come along

Proximity clustering means the human never has to pin everything, only the anchors.

Annotated Snippets

Pin from an agent

mode defaults to "set", which replaces the whole list.

canvas_pin_nodes({ nodeIds: ["node-a", "node-b"], mode: "add" })

Read it back

Includes the neighbourhood for each pin.

resources/read canvas://pinned-context

FAQ

Does pinning move or lock the node?

No. Context pins are separate from arrange-locking; a pinned node still moves.

What happens when a pinned node is deleted?

The pin is dropped with it — pins always resolve to live nodes.

Is there a limit?

Twenty pins. Past that, curation stops being curation.

Glossary

Context pin

A human-curated marker that puts a node into the agent’s context.

Neighbourhood

The unpinned nodes spatially near a pin, surfaced alongside it.

Reading order

Nodes sorted top-left to bottom-right, the way a human scans a board.

Blank ext-app tiles on WebKit

Executive Summary

Several MCP App nodes rendered as black tiles after a cold reload in WebKit hosts. Content was present in the DOM but never composited.

Timeline

09:41

Report filed warn

Screenshot shows four black tiles after reload.

10:05

Reproduced warn

Only when several apps hydrate in the same frame.

10:52

Root cause found info

Burst hydration overwhelms the WebKit compositor.

Fix landed ok

Serialized, boot-aware remount queue; one app at a time.

12:53

Verified ok

Ten consecutive cold reloads, no black tiles.

Root Cause

A fixed-stagger remount was not boot-aware: each recovery remount reboots the app, so staggered remounts overlapped into a fresh burst and the per-node one-shot flag was already spent.

Release flow

loops back to step 1 · max 3 runs

Run the flow

A step is queued once — after that its status control advances it (todo → in-progress → done).

or run the whole flow as a bounded loop:

Steer

Queued for the agent's next turn — steering is recorded on the timeline, it does not wake a running agent.

Loop

run 0 of 0

Each run is its own work item. When you mark the current run done, the surface opens the next run and steers again — until the cap or Stop.

Loop control lives in this panel, so reloading it stops the loop — the work items stay as the durable record.

Materialize

Lays this flow out on the canvas: one markdown node per step, joined in order by flow edges, plus a dashed loop-back edge. Each step node gets its own work item, so its status chip tracks the agent.

Re-materializing REPLACES the nodes this panel put on the board — it never stacks a second copy. The work items it already created stay as the durable record.

step it is actually on.
